<?php

const MOD = 1000000007;

class ModInt {
    public int $v;

    public function __construct(int $n) {
        $this->v = $n % MOD;
        if ($this->v < 0) $this->v += MOD;
    }

    public static function new(int $n): ModInt {
        return new ModInt($n);
    }

    public static function zero(): ModInt {
        return new ModInt(0);
    }

    public static function one(): ModInt {
        return new ModInt(1);
    }

    public function add(ModInt $rhs): ModInt {
        $d = $this->v + $rhs->v;
        if ($d >= MOD) $d -= MOD;
        return new ModInt($d);
    }

    public function addAssign(ModInt $rhs): void {
        $this->v = $this->add($rhs)->v;
    }

    public function sub(ModInt $rhs): ModInt {
        $d = $this->v + MOD - $rhs->v;
        if ($d >= MOD) $d -= MOD;
        return new ModInt($d);
    }

    public function subAssign(ModInt $rhs): void {
        $this->v = $this->sub($rhs)->v;
    }

    public function mul(ModInt $rhs): ModInt {
        $d = (int)(((int)$this->v * (int)$rhs->v) % MOD);
        return new ModInt($d);
    }

    public function mulAssign(ModInt $rhs): void {
        $this->v = $this->mul($rhs)->v;
    }

    public function neg(): ModInt {
        if ($this->v == 0) return new ModInt(0);
        return new ModInt(MOD - $this->v);
    }

    public function pow(int $n): ModInt {
        $t = ModInt::one();
        $s = new ModInt($this->v);
        while ($n > 0) {
            if ($n & 1) {
                $t->mulAssign($s);
            }
            $s->mulAssign($s);
            $n >>= 1;
        }
        return $t;
    }

    public function inv(): ModInt {
        return $this->pow(MOD - 2);
    }

    public static function comb(int $n, int $k): ModInt {
        if ($k > $n) {
            return ModInt::zero();
        }
        $k = min($k, $n - $k);
        $nu = ModInt::one();
        $de = ModInt::one();
        for ($i = 0; $i < $k; $i++) {
            $nu->mulAssign(new ModInt($n - $i));
            $de->mulAssign(new ModInt($i + 1));
        }
        return $nu->mul($de->inv());
    }
}

class Precalc {
    public array $inv;
    public array $fact;
    public array $ifact;

    public function __construct(int $n) {
        $this->inv = array_fill(0, $n + 1, ModInt::one());
        $this->fact = array_fill(0, $n + 1, ModInt::one());
        $this->ifact = array_fill(0, $n + 1, ModInt::one());
        for ($i = 2; $i <= $n; $i++) {
            $this->inv[$i] = (new ModInt(-$this->inv[MOD % $i]->v))->mul(new ModInt(intdiv(MOD, $i)));
            $this->fact[$i] = $this->fact[$i - 1]->mul(new ModInt($i));
            $this->ifact[$i] = $this->ifact[$i - 1]->mul($this->inv[$i]);
        }
    }

    public function invVal(int $n): ModInt {
        return $this->inv[$n];
    }

    public function factVal(int $n): ModInt {
        return $this->fact[$n];
    }

    public function ifactVal(int $n): ModInt {
        return $this->ifact[$n];
    }

    public function comb(int $n, int $k): ModInt {
        if ($k > $n) {
            return ModInt::zero();
        }
        return $this->fact[$n]->mul($this->ifact[$k])->mul($this->ifact[$n - $k]);
    }
}

function run() {
    $line = trim(fgets(STDIN));
    $parts = preg_split('/\s+/', $line);
    $n = intval($parts[0]);
    $k = intval($parts[1]);
    $pc = new Precalc(50);
    $ans = ModInt::one();
    $d = 2;
    while ((int)$d * (int)$d <= $n) {
        if ($n % $d == 0) {
            $c = 0;
            while ($n % $d == 0) {
                $c++;
                $n = intdiv($n, $d);
            }
            $dp = array_fill(0, $c + 1, ModInt::zero());
            $dp[$c] = ModInt::one();
            for ($iter = 0; $iter < $k; $iter++) {
                $next = array_fill(0, $c + 1, ModInt::zero());
                for ($i = 0; $i <= $c; $i++) {
                    $tmp = $dp[$i]->mul($pc->invVal($i + 1));
                    $next[$i]->addAssign($tmp);
                }
                for ($i = $c - 1; $i >= 0; $i--) {
                    $next[$i] = $next[$i]->add($next[$i + 1]);
                }
                $dp = $next;
            }
            $s = ModInt::zero();
            $f = 1;
            for ($i = 0; $i <= $c; $i++) {
                $s->addAssign(new ModInt($f % MOD)->mul($dp[$i]));
                $f *= $d;
            }
            $ans->mulAssign($s);
        }
        $d++;
    }
    if ($n > 1) {
        $p = $pc->invVal(2)->pow($k);
        $one = ModInt::one();
        $term1 = $one->sub($p);
        $term2 = (new ModInt($n % MOD))->mul($p);
        $ans->mulAssign($term1->add($term2));
    }
    echo $ans->v . PHP_EOL;
}

source_data.prob_desc_description: Makoto has a big blackboard with a positive integer $$$n$$$ written on it. He will perform the following action exactly $$$k$$$ times:Suppose the number currently written on the blackboard is $$$v$$$. He will randomly pick one of the divisors of $$$v$$$ (possibly $$$1$$$ and $$$v$$$) and replace $$$v$$$ with this divisor. As Makoto uses his famous random number generator (RNG) and as he always uses $$$58$$$ as his generator seed, each divisor is guaranteed to be chosen with equal probability.He now wonders what is the expected value of the number written on the blackboard after $$$k$$$ steps.It can be shown that this value can be represented as $$$\frac{P}{Q}$$$ where $$$P$$$ and $$$Q$$$ are coprime integers and $$$Q \not\equiv 0 \pmod{10^9+7}$$$. Print the value of $$$P \cdot Q^{-1}$$$ modulo $$$10^9+7$$$.
source_data.prob_desc_output_spec: Print a single integer — the expected value of the number on the blackboard after $$$k$$$ steps as $$$P \cdot Q^{-1} \pmod{10^9+7}$$$ for $$$P$$$, $$$Q$$$ defined above.
source_data.prob_desc_input_spec: The only line of the input contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$k$$$ ($$$1 \leq n \leq 10^{15}$$$, $$$1 \leq k \leq 10^4$$$).
source_data.prob_desc_notes: NoteIn the first example, after one step, the number written on the blackboard is $$$1$$$, $$$2$$$, $$$3$$$ or $$$6$$$ — each occurring with equal probability. Hence, the answer is $$$\frac{1+2+3+6}{4}=3$$$.In the second example, the answer is equal to $$$1 \cdot \frac{9}{16}+2 \cdot \frac{3}{16}+3 \cdot \frac{3}{16}+6 \cdot \frac{1}{16}=\frac{15}{8}$$$.
